analysis.title: International Market Intelligence - Morning Briefing (Nov 1, 2026)
key_insights: APAC markets are up on the open with rotation from defensives into cyclicals. Brent is below $110 on reports that Trump is giving Iran diplomacy more time, and China held market support meetings (STAR50 +3.5%). Weekend AI headlines were net negative (capital raising, circular financing, legal issues).

Global hedge funds fell about 3.5% in October. JPM Positioning Intelligence does not call the de-risking capitulatory, but expects alpha could rebound because similar alpha drawdowns have tended to precede rebounds, de-grossing has been widespread (Multi-Strats especially), and Momentum exposure is about 30% of its peak.

US midterms: SPX has averaged +5.4%, +11.4%, +12.5% and +14.7% over 3, 6, 9 and 12 months after midterms since 1990, with a 100% positive hit rate at 6, 9 and 12 months. A Democratic sweep could be mildly dollar-bearish.
APAC clients are more bearish than US clients but less bearish than EU clients. Many are still up double digits on the year and lack incentive to re-engage until a clear trend emerges.

US consumer: the top 4 income quintiles hold 6%-27% more inflation-adjusted cash than at YE2019 (nearly $8T nominal). Retail sales run $723bn/month YTD2026 vs $505bn in 2019. Card delinquencies are normalizing to pre-COVID trends, not deteriorating. JPM sees no imminent consumer crack.

Consumer sub-sector views from clients: airlines, cruise and hotels have robust demand. Autos and homebuilders are rate-sensitive, so parts and suppliers may make more sense. Retailers face freight costs at 30-40% of total cost, with rates more than tripled YTD. Staples are most at risk of margin compression and likely a source of funds.
Corporate health: HY default rate is 2.7% vs a 3.2% long-term average, after about 20% of HY market cap was upgraded to IG post-COVID.

AI infrastructure credit: JPM TMT specialists say credit markets are becoming more discriminating but show no broader funding crisis. AI infrastructure has absorbed more than $500B of debt YTD (IG >$350B, leveraged >$60B, private credit about $100B+). Hyperscaler all-in funding costs are up about 120bps, and the HY compute index is +372bps YTD.

AI-related CDS spreads have widened on technical selling and hedging demand as banks buy protection on data center lending. This pushed CDS above cash-bond spreads, which JPM sees as attractive for investors willing to sell protection. CRWV has converts outstanding with CDS at a slightly positive basis.

IG TMT credit: MSFT, GOOGL and AMZN are fundamentally resilient. ORCL and SpaceX spreads widened on reports each is seeking off-balance-sheet financing. Erica Spear expects growing debt supply may pressure spreads into 2027. Nvidia is a key transmission channel for stress because of its ties to GPU customers including CRWV.

CRWV: JPM credit analyst Tom Egan calls it a financing challenge, not a solvency one. He projects last-12-month EBITDA rising from about $4.4B (June 2026) to $7.3B by year-end and nearly $20B by YE27, with about $130B of contracted revenue.

France/Europe contagion: JPM calls the concerns exaggerated, with a roughly 3% primary deficit and debt/GDP near 120% vs a 180% threshold 10-15 years away. OATs discount debt/GDP above 150% and an implied deficit above 8%. JPM sees room for relief into year-end around the budget discussion but no material reversal until 2Q27 elections.
EU Banks: JPM says the earnings trend is unchanged and dips of more than 15% vs the index should be bought. Call ratio spreads and call spreads are attractive.

Midterm implications: a federal AI law is unlikely (veto, no 2/3 majority). If Democrats take the House, they could defund Middle East military efforts. Tariff policy is unlikely to change. Longer-dated bonds could see a bid if Democrats halt deficit spending.

Treasuries: before the Oct 22 rally, JPM's view was that 5.50% was more likely than 5.00% for the 10Y yield. The market prices a hike in Dec 2026 and two in FY27. Clients see upside risk to that pricing, and the downside risk is a near-term end to the US/Iran conflict with oil normalizing (low conviction).

AI/tech pushback points: semis revenue driven by supply-constrained price spikes, neocloud turmoil and bankruptcy risk, and software being less of a funding source. A buy needs a positioning flush, hyperscaler capex confirmation, semis earnings, tighter credit and positive seasonality, which JPM says points to early November if it occurs.

Broadening: since the July 28 lows SPX is +4.8% (through Oct 22), but more than half of the index has a negative return and 69% of stocks lag the SPX. Of about 65% of SPX companies mentioning AI operational improvement in 26Q2, fewer than 5% quantified the impact.

Cyclicals: client interest centers on financials (GSIBs, credit cards). Aero/Def has a negative client outlook on the risk a Blue Wave halts military funding. Clients view the dollar as range-bound and likely at a local high, copper bullish on China growth, and silver as part of the AI trade.

JPM Market Intelligence is tactically bullish on global equities, preferring long US and Asia (Japan, Korea, Taiwan) vs EU. Longs: infrastructure and less-levered hyperscalers, EU and JA banks, EU industrials, EU miners, EU pharma, UKX. Shorts: AI-vulnerable ex-software, short-cycle data center capex names, EU insurance, autos, chemicals, Asian consumer electronics, medtech, MDAX.
EM: JPM is bullish. Tactical longs are China STAR50 vs KWEB, Korea vs Southeast Asia, and Taiwan. Hedges are long Brazil (EWZ) ahead of the end-of-month runoff and EEM for broadening.

Positioning Intelligence: US Tactical Positioning Monitor is at the 33rd percentile, retail sentiment at the 6th percentile, and CTA US equity positioning at the 44th percentile. The Split Congress pair (JPMSC26P) is at 2-year highs. US banks have a strong November seasonal record.

TMT vs Defensives sentiment gap and social media sentiment are both at the 6th percentile, similar to prior episodes (Mar 2026, Mar/Apr 2025, Aug/Sep 2024, Apr 2024, Dec 2022) that were followed by Tech-led rebounds.

HFs flipped to buying Biotech and Med Tech. Utilities rallied but HFs kept selling, leaving them with the lowest net positioning of any major industry. EU positioning rebounded from the 5th to the 14th percentile. China/HK positioning is the most bearish of any region at the 5th percentile.

Clients said recent airline, cruise and hotel earnings and management commentary confirmed robust demand despite higher prices.

vol_and_positioning: Positioning Intelligence does not classify October's de-risking as capitulatory. Lingering risks are potential quant de-grossing and elevated US Tech flows and futures positioning.
Momentum exposure is about 30% of its peak and at more than 12-month lows. Prior -3z events in the 20d long-short spread saw positive forward 20d spreads in 6 of 7 cases (average +1%).

US Tactical Positioning Monitor is at the 33rd percentile (Oct 29) with a neutral 4-week change. Retail sentiment is at the 6th percentile, ETF flows are +1z and CTA US equity positioning is at the 44th percentile.
EU positioning rose from the 5th to the 14th percentile. China/HK positioning is at the 5th percentile, the most bearish of any major region.
Option hedges: keep MCX < UKX until spending clarity emerges, and short France vs EU Domestics. Call ratio spreads and call spreads are attractive on EU Banks.
The Split Congress pair (JPMSC26P) is at 2-year highs, with HFs more bullish on Split Congress longs via short covering.
geopolitical: Reports that Trump is giving Iran diplomacy more time, with resumption of combat operations as the consensus expectation.
US/Iran conflict: a near-term end could normalize oil, refined product, petrochemical and shipping and insurance rates.
Concerns about Middle East escalation after the US midterm elections.
If Democrats take the House, they could defund military efforts in the Middle East and force an off-ramp for Trump.
Tariff policy is unlikely to change after the midterms given the President's latitude on foreign policy.
France fiscal concerns and the EU sovereign spread tape echoing 2011-12.
cross_bank_references: Agreed with the JPM bull case on copper (client feedback, JPM view).
JPM Credit Analyst Tom Egan and TMT specialist views are cited within this JPM note.

tension_points.bull_case: Hyperscalers are fundamentally well-positioned, capital remains available and CRWV is a financing challenge rather than a solvency issue, with projected EBITDA rising to nearly $20B by YE27.
tension_points.bear_case: Leveraged GPU and data center developers face tighter financing, growing debt supply may pressure spreads into 2027, and circular financing through Nvidia concentrates correlated downside risk.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Further widening of spreads on externally financed names such as ORCL or CRWV, or failure to deliver contracted compute capacity on schedule.

tension_points.bull_case: SPX has risen after every midterm over 6, 9 and 12 months since 1990, and prior -3z alpha drawdowns saw positive forward spreads in 6 of 7 cases.
tension_points.bear_case: The de-risking was not capitulatory, with potential quant de-grossing, elevated US Tech positioning and Middle East escalation risk after the midterms.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Quant de-grossing or a capitulation event that has not yet occurred, or escalation in the Middle East after the midterms.

tension_points.bull_case: Strong household and corporate balance sheets, accelerating growth and inflation point to upside risk to the priced Dec 2026 hike and two FY27 hikes.
tension_points.bear_case: A near-term end to the US/Iran conflict and quick normalization of oil and shipping costs could mean fewer hikes than priced (low conviction).
tension_points.what_invalidates: A near-term end to the US/Iran conflict followed by quick normalization of oil, refined product, petrochemical and shipping and insurance rates.

tension_points.bull_case: France's fiscal problem is idiosyncratic, with debt/GDP near 120% against a 180% threshold, and the ECB backstop limits disorderly spread widening.
tension_points.bear_case: HF crowding and a 60% non-resident ownership of French debt worsened the move, and the tape echoes the 2011-12 sovereign crisis.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Disorderly spread widening if the ECB backstop (TPI, OMT) is not activated.
